author: yhk1038
body:
## Problem

Empty bordered boxes appear in the transcript while a turn is streaming — often
a run of them, and often where a tool card should be. Reloading the session
makes them go away and renders the content correctly in its right place, which
narrows the fault to how the live view assembles messages rather than to the
data itself.

## Root cause

A `tool_use` block's arguments stream in as `input_json_delta`, buffered and
applied on the next animation frame. Measured against a live CLI, the
`assistant` event for the same turn arrives *before* that frame runs: it
flushes the buffer, then replaces the turn's blocks with its own payload.

That payload is emitted mid-turn and can still carry an empty `input`, so the
arguments the stream had already assembled were overwritten with nothing. The
JSONL restore path never runs this replacement, which is why a reload looks
fine.

The reporter's analysis pointed at `UserMessageRenderer` missing the
empty-content guard that `AssistantMessageRenderer` has. That observation is
accurate, but it turned out not to be what shows on screen: an empty
`MessageBox` collapses to no visible height, and adding a guard there would
have hidden entries `mergeToolResults` deliberately keeps visible.

## Fix

Keep whichever side actually has arguments — an empty `input` in the final
payload no longer clobbers what was streamed, while a populated one still
wins. The flush also resolves its target `tool_use` by id instead of by the
active block index, which the same `assistant` event resets.

## Also here: copying the front-end log

Diagnosing this took several rounds of asking for console output, which first
means walking a reporter through opening devtools — and anything that scrolled
past is already gone.

`LogForwarder` already intercepts `console.*` from startup; it now also keeps
the last 5000 lines. **Copy plugin front log** in the palette's Support section
puts that whole history on the clipboard and confirms with a toast, so a
reporter can attach it without opening the inspector. The same history is
reachable from the console via `window.ccgLogs`. Search-only — it is a
diagnostics aid, not an everyday action.

## Verification

- New regression test fails before the fix (`expected {} to deeply equal
  { file_path: '/tmp/a.txt' }`) and passes after
- Webview 1803 passed, backend 1044 passed, Kotlin passed, typecheck clean
- Palette entry driven end to end in a browser: hidden until searched, listed
  above **View help docs**, toast shown, clipboard verified against a sentinel

One limit worth stating plainly: the race did not reproduce in the two live
browser runs after the fix, so the evidence for the fix is the regression test,
not a before/after observation on screen.

Closes #232

author: dmadisetti
body:
The acceptance gate has never been green. The post-reboot phase failed because the smoke's own `nix-store --gc` collected the seeded-but-unrooted rebuild inputs (`virtualisation.additionalPaths` registers paths in the guest Nix DB but roots nothing), so re-realising the disposable rootfs degraded into an offline world-rebuild that died on the first fetched dependency — the xz/zlib cascade in the CI log.

Two changes to `imageless-cri-vm`:

- Root the `.drv` closure and all build-time outputs (`smoke-rootfs.inputDerivation`) through `system.extraDependencies`, which the system profile GC-roots. The rootfs **output** stays unrooted on purpose: it is the disposable path whose collection the gate asserts.
- `writableStoreUseTmpfs = false`: with the default tmpfs upper layer, the pre-reboot rootfs vanished with the reboot itself, so the "GC reclaims it after reboot" assertion passed vacuously. On the VM disk the old rootfs survives the reboot and the assertion actually exercises GC.

## 캡처하다 발견한 결함 — 근거 조문이 틀리게 나왔습니다

녹취 의무(REC-001)의 **최우선 근거로 제28조(자료의 기록 및 유지·관리) 대신 제18조(적정성원칙)** 가 표시됐습니다. 조문을 근거로 내세우는 도구에서 틀린 조문이 맨 앞에 오는 건 단순 버그가 아니라 신뢰를 깎는 문제입니다.

원인은 두 군데였습니다.

1. **`search_chunks()`** — 규칙마다 손으로 매핑해 둔 근거 조문에 가산점(`+5.0`)만 주고 있어 BM25 점수가 높은 다른 조문에 밀렸습니다. 지정 조문을 별도 목록으로 모아 앞에 두도록 바꿨습니다.
2. **`find_legal_basis()`** — 1번을 고쳐도 라이브 원문 보강(`allow_live=True`)을 켜면 `_deduplicate([*live, *local])` 이 라이브 결과를 앞에 붙여 순서가 다시 뒤집혔습니다. 병합 후에도 지정 조문이 먼저 오도록 정렬합니다.

**검증 — 라이브 보강을 켠 상태에서 규칙 8종 전부 의도한 조문이 최우선입니다.**

| 규칙 | 최우선 근거 |
|---|---|
| PKG-001 / EXP-001 / DATE-001 / ACK-001 | 금소법 제19조 (설명의무) |
| FIT-001 | 제17조 (적합성원칙) |
| ADV-001 | 제21조 (부당권유 금지) |
| DOC-001 | 제23조 (계약서류 제공) |

author: dammianmiller
body:
## What monitoring found

No 401s, no errors, no exceptions — the auth and timeout fixes hold. But the llama server was **thrashing its host-RAM prompt cache**.

That cache holds KV prefixes so a follow-up turn re-uses its prompt instead of re-prefilling it. Undersize it and every eviction turns the next turn on that prefix into a full reprocess.

## Measured — one hour of a live agent session at `--cache-ram 16384`

| | |
|---|---|
| evictions | **27** (~23.5 GB churned, avg entry 869 MiB) |
| large reprocesses (>5k tok) | **30** |
| tokens re-prefilled | **829,587** |
| time lost | **418s of 482s total prefill — 87%** |
| worst single stall | **44.4s** |

Eviction count and large-reprocess count track ~1:1 — that's the causal link, not a coincidence: the cache was holding a working set **1.5× its size**, so entries were evicted before they could be re-used.

## Change

`--cache-ram 16384 → 32768`, which clears the measured ~23.5 GB with margin.

Host has 121 GB with ~50 GB available and **zero swap in use**, so this leaves ~18 GB free. Sized to the *measured working set* rather than to all free RAM, because this cache competes with the page cache and with whatever else the operator runs.

The Gemma profile moves too — its `8192` was llama.cpp's **default**, never a choice, and the working set is the *session's* rather than the model's, so the same figure applies.

## Notes

Config only, no code. Takes effect on the next llama-server restart, which is operator-gated by `enforcement-infra-protect` — correctly, and including via a script since v1.172.7.

Re-measure before raising further:

```
journalctl --user -u uap-llama-server.service --since "60 min ago" | grep -c "making room for prompt cache"
```

Expert review waived (`UAP_NO_REVIEW`) per a session constraint on spawning agents.

author: nmorabowen
body:
## What

`formEAStrue`'s inner-Newton convergence test could never pass when the loop starts from an already-converged enhanced state — which happens on **every assembly**, since the routine re-enters from both `update()` and `formResidAndTangent`. Observed on the ADR-79 bearing campaign eas runs: `||r|| = 1.4e-12` tested against `r0 = 8.4e-15` — noise compared to noise — emitting a warning **per element per global iteration**. A 6-step probe wrote 37 MB of log; the queued 2000-step run projected ~12 GB. It also burned the full 12 inner iterations (× 8 GPs of `setTrialStrain`/`getTangent`) on every assembly, inflating eas per-step cost.

## Why it could never pass

1. The `count >= 1` guard forbade declaring convergence at entry, forcing a Newton step with a pure-roundoff RHS that lands at the material-evaluation noise floor.
2. The fallback floor `tolAbs = 1e-12` is absolute in force×length² units — the exact units mistake the adjacent comment warns about for the *relative* tolerance. For large-unit (SI steel/soil) models the noise floor sits above it, so the test degenerates to an unreachable absolute test.

## Fix (both elements, identical structure)

- Test convergence from `count == 0` — a converged entry exits before the noise step.
- Scale-aware noise floor `tolNoise * rScale`, with `rScale = Σ_GP ||M^T σ dV||` — the magnitude of the terms whose cancellation produces `residE`; below ~1e-12 of that the residual is roundoff, not signal.
- Silent stagnation break (`r >= rPrev && r <= r0`): a step that fails to reduce the residual while no worse than entry means roundoff dominates — accept best-available alpha (the same acceptance the maxIters path already makes) without the wasted iterations or the warning.

The maxIters warning is kept for genuine divergence.

## Tests

- New SI-scale (200 GPa elastic) regressions on the distorted hex/quad assert **no** `did not converge` output across a multi-step Newton run. Elastic on purpose: upstream `J2Plasticity`'s tangent gives the inner Newton a slow *linear* rate, so its maxIters warnings are honest — a separate, material-side issue, out of scope here.
- Full brick+quad sweep: **192 passed** (all 24 pre-existing eas tests untouched and green).
- Quirks ledger entry added (relative-test-with-count-guard + absolute-floor-units gotcha).

## 1. Camino de entrada (`fbbadec`)

El motor migró de SQLite/efímero a Postgres+Redis+worker; el camino de entrada no. Cada hallazgo era una reliquia asomando por una superficie de usuario.

- `RuntimeError` en `storage/factory.py` escapaba el handler del CLI → traceback. Ahora una línea, exit 2.
- "Postgres no está corriendo" (el fallo #1 de un primer run) salía como ~15 líneas de psycopg. Traducido con hint accionable.
- `active_consumers()` existía **con tests** y `cmd_run` no lo llamaba: un run sin worker esperaba 600s en silencio. Ahora falla en milisegundos.
- `.env.example` (`/15`) y `docker-compose.yml` (`/0`) apuntaban a Redis DBs distintas — el mismo bug que el README advierte en negrita.
- Purga de `--no-persist`: 14 superficies, ~30 ocurrencias. Tres tests **exigían** que el CLI imprimiera el comando inválido.
- `Dockerfile` era-SQLite; el worker se construía sin el extra `redis` que necesita para existir.
- **5 tests de Arena rotos en `main`**: no era Arena. `run_launcher` elige dispatch por entorno, así que con `SELFEVALS_REDIS_URL` presente encolaban sin worker. Verdes en shell limpio, colgados tras `source .env`. Fixture autouse que aísla la suite del entorno.
- README: el Quickstart prometía 3 comandos y explotaba en el tercero; además el camino `pip install` no lleva a ningún lado (`docker-compose.yml` no va en el paquete). Ahora lo dice.

## 2. `search_space.agents` — el eje de binding (`6a1dc5e`)

`build_adapter` se llamaba una vez por experimento, **fuera del loop**. Eso hacía inexpresable comparar Twilio vs Retell, LangChain vs Mastra o workflow vs agente: difieren antes de la primera request.

Ahora un experimento declara bloques `agent:` completos y el executor resuelve el adapter por propuesta, con caché. Cada variante recalcula su bucket de rate-limit por proveedor.

De paso, `editable.model_choice` por fin *hace* algo: antes solo podía rechazar.

Ejemplo ejecutable (`selfevals examples copy bakeoff`), verificado end-to-end: premium `pass@1=1` keep, budget `pass@1=0.5` reject, costo por iteración. **Sin una sola rama de git.**

## 3. Auth (`07814a9`, `2327302`, `c490f62`, `1c1e1b7`)

Research previo descartó Better Auth: es TypeScript-only, así que con FastAPI significaría un tercer servicio y la identidad partida en dos schemas. Langfuse — mismo modelo de distribución — resolvió esto con auth embebido. Ese es el camino.

**Tres agujeros que fallaban en abierto:**
- Un typo en `SELFEVALS_AUTH_MODE` degradaba a "confía en el header". Ahora es error de arranque.
- `POST /api/workspaces` otorgaba los 6 roles al creador, incluido `auditor`.
- **Un `user_id` con punto rompía sus propios tokens** — o sea, cualquier email.

**Identidad real:** `users`, `user_sessions` (guarda el *hash* del token, así que un dump no entrega sesiones) y `api_keys` como carril propio. Login/logout/me/logout-everywhere.

**Membresías**, que era el bloqueante real del multi-usuario: no había forma de invitar a nadie salvo SQL a mano. Dos invariantes: solo admins gestionan miembros, y no se puede quitar al último admin (nada puede restaurarlo).

**Frontend:** `fetch` omitía cookies, así que con login habilitado toda request llegaría sin autenticar — silenciosamente, porque en `local` nada se enforcea.

## Correcciones durante la implementación

- Mi regex de email aceptaba `a..b@x.com`, `.a@x.com` y `a@-x.com`. Reemplazado por `EmailStr`.
- `Secure` incondicional en la cookie rompía `selfevals serve` local: el browser la acepta y nunca la reenvía. El login parecía funcionar y no pegaba.

## Dependencias nuevas (aprobadas)

`argon2-cffi` y `email-validator`, ambas en el extra `[web]`.

## Verificación

1524 tests (desde 1457), ruff, mypy --strict, `npm run check` 0 errores, audit sin regresión. Quickstart recorrido end-to-end: ~1s con worker vivo.

Baseline de deuda actualizado una vez, con revisión: +2 `get_entity_calls` y +2 `list_entities_calls` por los endpoints de membresía — uso previsto de esas APIs.

Deuxième des quatre tranches du **lot 1** (#2351), toujours **sans IHM** : le calcul du tableau que l'écran et la CLI afficheront tous deux — ils ne peuvent donc pas diverger.

## Contacts **et** fichiers distincts
Deux cents contacts sur **deux** fichiers ne racontent pas la même nuit que deux cents contacts sur **cent cinquante**. Le premier cas peut être un individu qui chasse devant le micro ; le second, une activité diffuse toute la nuit.

Le référentiel compare des **contacts** — c'est son unité. Les fichiers, comptés à part, disent si ces contacts sont **concentrés**.

## « Validées seulement » recalcule, ne masque pas
Une espèce dont aucune observation n'est validée **sort** du tableau ; les contacts des autres **baissent**, ce qui change leur **classe d'activité**.

C'est le but : lire la nuit telle que Tadarida la propose, puis telle qu'on l'a soi-même validée, et **voir l'écart**. Un masquage laisserait les classes inchangées — et mentirait.

## Une cellule sans classe dit pourquoi

| Cas | Ce qui s'écrit |
|---|---|
| Orthoptère, oiseau, bruit | « Non couvert par le référentiel » |
| Chiroptère sans seuil pour ce contexte | « Pas de seuil pour ce contexte » |
| Seuils peu fiables, faute de mieux | « Moyenne **(indicatif)** » |

Une cellule blanche se lirait comme une donnée manquante, alors que l'absence a ici **trois** sens distincts.

## Une visibilité élargie, et pourquoi
`ReferentielActivite.lire(Reader)` devient publique. Non pour ouvrir une porte aux tests, mais parce que **le format est le contrat** : c'est par là qu'un référentiel fourni par l'utilisateur entrerait un jour, et par là que les tests des couches supérieures se donnent des seuils **explicites** — un test de règle qui lit les vraies données se met à échouer quand la source évolue, pour des raisons étrangères à la règle qu'il vérifie. La justesse de la ressource est gardée à part.

## Vérification
- 6 tests : comptage, fichiers distincts, recalcul de la bascule, séquence non identifiée écartée, classe et quantiles, hors référentiel, nuit sans validation.
- Garde-fou : la bascule neutralisée fait rougir **deux** tests (`Expecting empty but was: […]`, `Expected size: 1 but was: 2`).
- Portail qualité vert, cliquets ADR verts.

body:
## Summary

Fixes #1729.

`babysit_resolve_thread.py`'s thread-resolution-scope classifier (`project_thread`'s `botOnly` computation) inspects every fetched comment in a review thread, not just the opener, to decide `botOnly` -- correct for catching a genuine human reply. But the worker's own documented reply to a bot thread (a classification reply, a `Fixed in <sha>` follow-up -- `reference/orchestration.md`) is *also* a real API comment, posted under the worker's own login, not the bot's.

Before this fix: replying to a bot thread flipped `botOnly` false the moment the reply posted (indistinguishable from a genuine third-party human joining). `classify()`'s bright line then fires -- `if not thread["botOnly"] and not include_human: return "skipped-human-thread"` -- and `--include-human` is unset by design in worker/safe modes (must never touch a genuine human thread), so nothing lifts it back in. The thread is permanently stranded outside BOTH resolution scopes, even though replying to it was exactly the correct, expected action.

## Fix

- **`--self-logins`** (new flag, mirroring `babysit_merge.py`'s existing flag of the same name, and the already-configured-but-never-threaded `babysit_self_logins` userConfig key). `project_thread`'s `botOnly` now treats a self-login-authored comment as a third admissible authorship alongside bot and third-party human: neutral for `botOnly` (does not disqualify it, unlike a genuine human reply) but not sufficient to earn it alone -- a thread still needs at least one ACTUAL bot comment to be `botOnly`.
- **Second-order fix, found during review**: fixing `botOnly` alone isn't enough. The mandated classification-reply table (`reference/review-discipline.md`) restates the source finding's own severity marker (e.g. a `CRITICAL` column, or "VALID -- not a security concern") as part of the worker's own reply -- so a raw severity scan over that self-reply would re-trip `--autonomous`'s `skipped-severity-marked` guard the instant `botOnly` stopped blocking it, just moving the stranding to a different verdict. The severity scan now strips a self-authored comment's classification-table rows (not its whole body) before scanning, reusing `babysit_classify.count_findings`'s identical existing rule (the helper is promoted from private to shared rather than reimplemented) -- non-table self content still flags.
- Every copyable resolve-thread command form (`SKILL.md`, `reference/safety.md` x3, `reference/orchestration.md` x2) now carries `--self-logins @me,<self-logins>` alongside `--extra-bot-logins`, verified by this repo's own `test_every_documented_wrapper_command` doc-parser-conformance gate.
- `plugin.json`'s `babysit_self_logins` description now names the resolve-thread bot-only test among the surfaces the self set covers.
- CHANGELOG entry + patch version bump (0.34.0 -> 0.34.1, renumbered from 0.33.3 when main shipped 0.34.0 and its own 0.33.3 entry), matching this plugin's changelog-parity CI gate.

## Test plan

- [x] `python -m unittest discover` over `plugins/source-control/skills/babysit-prs/scripts/tests` -- 453 tests, all green (includes 11 new regression tests: the bug reproduced without `--self-logins`, the fix proven with it, a self-only thread still correctly not `botOnly`, a genuine third-party human still blocking `botOnly` regardless of `--self-logins`, truncation still failing closed, the severity-scan re-stranding scenario reproduced and fixed, non-table self content still flagging, third-party severity markers still flagging, and a full end-to-end `--autonomous --only-outdated` run in the exact tier the bug occurs in).
- [x] `test_guards.py`'s guard-contract suite (including `test_reference_doc_matches_the_tables` and `test_every_documented_wrapper_command`) -- green, no `guard_contract.py` changes needed since `classify()`'s predicate contract (which takes `botOnly` as an input) is unchanged.
- [x] `plugins/skill-quality/scripts/check-skill.sh babysit-prs` -- PASS, 0 errors (SKILL.md at 497/500 lines).
- [x] `scripts/check-changelog-parity.sh --check` -- passes.
- [x] `markdownlint-cli2` over every changed `.md` file -- 0 issues.

## Related

- Closes #1729
- Refs #571 -- the adjacent, still-open gap in the same `--autonomous` resolve path: the per-thread
  comment pins do not stop a worker's own push from displacing a thread. This PR fixes the
  authorship-classification half of the stranding; #571 tracks the `isOutdated` pinning half.
- Refs #1703 -- the sibling fix in the same plugin for how a declared non-structural account is
  classified, the same identity-classification family as `--self-logins` here.

운영자 SaaS 구현 **세션 ①**. 🔴 **머니 경로** — staging 실결제 통과 전 세션 ② 착수 금지.

**3줄 보고**: (a) 소비자 레일만(도매 무접촉) (b) 머니 경로 **접촉**(결제 금액 산출, 단 **새 요율 로직 0**) (c) 롤백 = gb 블록 3곳 제거 → `product.price` 환원

---

## 문제

`resolveGbPricing`이 `gb-marketplace.routes.ts`(표시)에만 쓰여 **공구가로 결제되지 않았다** — 화면엔 특가, 결제는 상시가.

## 수정 — `order.routes.ts` 서버 권위 단가에 배선

- 루프 전 `getGbSessions` **배치 조회**(N+1 회피) + `gbViaRef`(linkOnly 세션용, 기존 ref 소스와 동일)
- 단가 = `resolveGbPricing(...).effectivePrice` + 옵션조정
- **fail-soft**: 세션 조회 실패 시 상시가로 진행(주문을 막지 않음)

**안전 방향**: `validateGbSession`이 `gb_price < 상시가`를 강제하고 `resolveGbPricing`도 `gbPrice < list`일 때만 적용 ⇒ **이 배선은 가격을 낮추기만 하고 올릴 수 없다.**

---

## 🔴 배선하며 드러난 것 — 이 레포엔 공구 할인이 **두 가지**다

| | 모델 | 상태 |
|---|---|---|
| ① | `group_buy_tiers` + `maxTierDiscount` | **이미 결제에 배선돼 있음** (`groupBuyCap` 서버 cap 재계산) |
| ② | `gb_price` (`product_supply_meta`) | 표시 전용이었음 |

둘 다 가진 상품에 ②를 단가에 얹으면, ①의 `perUnit`이 **이미 낮아진 `unit_price`** 에서 다시 계산돼 **cap이 부풀고 이중 할인(과소청구)** 이 된다.

⇒ 공구가가 적용된 상품은 `groupBuyCap` 누적에서 제외(`gbAppliedIds` → `continue`). **이 한 줄이 빠지면 돈이 샌다.**

---

## 테스트 — `gb-price-payment-wiring.test.ts` (10건)

- **순수 모델**: 특가 적용 / 상한(특가가 상시가보다 높아도 상시가) / 종료·미시작 / linkOnly는 ref 경유만
- **유어딜 순수취 == 정확히 5%**: 플랫폼 분은 **실제 결제액** 기준 — 상시가 10,000·결제 7,000이면 **350원**(500원 아님). 인플루언서 몫이 커져도 **플랫폼 분 불변**(먼저 떼고 나머지를 나눔). 합계가 결제액과 정확히 일치(원 단위 누수 0)
- **새 요율 로직 유입 차단**: `order.routes`에 플랫폼 요율 리터럴 없음
- **이중 할인 차단** 3종

**되돌려-검증**: 이중할인 차단 제거 / fail-soft 제거 / 요율 리터럴 유입 → **전부 빨강 확인 후 복원**.

---

## ⚠️ staging 실결제 검증 (세션 ② 착수 전 필수 — 세션이 못 함)

1. 공구 live 상품 구매 → 결제 금액이 **공구가**인지(상시가 아님)
2. `group_buy_tiers`도 가진 상품 → **이중 할인 없이** 공구가 그대로인지
3. 공구 종료 후 → 상시가 복귀
4. linkOnly: 직접 진입=상시가 / `?ref` 경유=공구가
5. 원장에서 **플랫폼 분 = 결제액의 5%**(상시가 5% 아님)

body:
> 🤖 SPARQ agent

Fixes #4984

**Head SHA:** `69e1721ca9e75e20619efcda1ba277ad369d03fd`

## Why this is time-boxed to tonight

`selection-alarm` was **inert** until PR #4982 merged at **05:01Z today**: its job `if:`
admitted only `conclusion == 'failure'`, while a fail-fast nightly concludes `cancelled`
(35 `cancelled` / 7 `success` / 3 `failure` all-time; 266 of 267 alarm runs job-SKIPPED;
last action 2026-07-19). #4982 moved admission into the script over the real jobs API, so
**it will fire again at the next nightly** (`17 3 * * *` on `ci.yml`).

Its backstop is **28 days stale** — last green nightly 2026-07-01 — so the first real
firing renders **644 / 579 / 554** suspect PRs in **18,064 / 16,329 / 15,755-char** bodies
(MEASURED against real nightly `30333511110`).

**Dedupe is per-key, so the first render of a key is the only render.** Whatever body
lands persists; a later cap will not rewrite it.

Verified against the authoritative source — `open_issue_exists()` lists `--state open`
only, so I enumerated the live body markers rather than titles or an all-states listing
(my first pass used `--state all` and got this wrong):

| dedupe key | measured suspects | open issue? | next nightly |
|---|---|---|---|
| `crate:sparq-fedplan` | **644** (18,064 chars) | none | **mints fresh** |
| `crate:sparq-reason` | **554** (15,755 chars) | #3614 **CLOSED** 2026-07-28 | **mints fresh** |
| `crate:sparq-mpc` | 579 (16,329 chars) | #3613 open | deduped, skipped |
| `crate:sparq-core` | — | #3612 open | deduped, skipped |

So **two** of the three measured findings render for the first and only time at the next
nightly, not one. A closed issue does not suppress its key.

## What this changes

The suspect set tracks the **age of the backstop**, not the size of the bug. 644 entries
is a *true* statement about a 28-day gap — the defect is that it is unreadable, not that
it is wrong. So this caps the **render only**:

- `correlate` still computes the **full** suspect set. The window is unchanged, the alarm
  is not suppressed, and dedupe keys are untouched.
- At most `MAX_RENDERED_SUSPECTS` (**20**) rows. The **omitted count**, the **total**, the
  **cap**, and the **ordering basis** are all stated in the body. Never a silent
  truncation.
- A list **at or under** the cap renders **in full with no omission notice**, so the cap
  cannot be satisfied by always truncating.

### Ordering basis

**Landing recency, newest first** — and it is the *input* order, not a re-sort: `git log`
is reverse-chronological, `window_commits` and `build_window` append in that order, and
`correlate` preserves it into `skip_to_prs[crate]` (and into the triage filter).

It is defensible rather than an arbitrary first-N: **every PR that landed after a given
suspect and that *affected* the failing crate re-ran that crate's lanes on a tree already
containing the suspect**, so the older a suspect is, the more independent chances its
breakage has already had to surface. The newest suspects have the least intervening
coverage.

That is a **prior, not an exoneration** — per-PR selected lanes are narrower than the
nightly full matrix, so an older suspect is not cleared. Which is exactly why the omitted
count is *stated* rather than dropped. `WindowCommit` carries no timestamp, so the render
cannot re-derive this ordering; `TestSuspectOrderIsLandingRecency` pins the invariant it
rests on.

### Measured result

| finding | before | after |
|---|---|---|
| `crate:` @ 644 suspects | 18,064 chars | **2,512** |
| `crate:` @ 2,300 suspects | > 65,536 (422) | **2,515** |
| `triage:` @ 644 suspects, 37-member workspace | — | **14,070** |

Body length **no longer tracks the window at all**: 644 vs 2,300 suspects differ by 3
chars — the digits of the printed total. The ~2,300-suspect hard failure against GitHub's
65,536-char limit is now unreachable.

## Verification

- **Control GREEN first**: 40 tests OK on the unmutated tree, *before* any mutation count
  was trusted. Sibling `test_alarm_lanes_non_gating.py` 9 OK; `test_banned_terminology.py`
  23 OK; `typos` rc=0.
- **Known positive**: the real **pre-fix** script (`git show origin/main:...`) dropped into
  the tree REDs **9** of the new tests. An instrument that cannot detect the actual,
  live defect cannot certify the fix.
- **15/15 mutants killed**, on **whole-tree** copies (the suite reads
  `.github/workflows/*`; a `scripts/`-only copy yields phantom kills). The harness refuses
  to score a mutant whose `sed` matched nothing, so a no-op cannot be counted as a kill.

| mutant | killed by |
|---|---|
| `no-cap-at-all` | 7 tests |
| `silent-truncation` (drop the notice) | 5 |
| `always-claim-omitted` | 2 — incl. the short-list pair |
| `keep-oldest-not-newest` | `..._keeps_the_NEWEST_suspects_not_an_arbitrary_slice` |
| `off-by-one-rows` | 6 |
| `wrong-omitted-count` | 6 |
| `hardcoded-tiny-cap` (`[:3]`) | 6 |
| `drop-negative-guard` | `..._never_drops_rows_on_a_nonsense_cap` |
| `drop-ordering-basis` / `drop-stale-backstop` / `drop-repro-hint` | `..._states_the_ordering_basis_and_the_real_cause` |
| `drop-total-in-header` | 2 |
| `correlate-resorts` / `triage-resorts` | the two order-preservation tests |
| `triage-drops-skipset` | 2 |

On expected values: the 644-suspect test asserts the literal **624** omitted (arithmetic
done in the test, not copied from the implementation) **and** that the disclosed count
equals `644 − rows actually rendered in the body`, so a body cannot state a bound it did
not honour. The row-counting extractor slices between two full, distinctive anchors via
`.index` (a rename REDs rather than returning a plausible empty list) and is
**validated against a known answer** — 3 suspects in, exactly 3 rows out — because a
row-count instrument that under-counts fails toward "the cap is working".

## What this does NOT fix

- **The 28-day-stale backstop.** Out of scope by design; filed as **#5025** with the
  measurement and the likely cause (fail-fast cancellation may make a run-level `success`
  structurally unreachable, so `last_green_nightly_sha()` is the last place still trusting
  the lossy aggregate #4982 moved off). This PR does **not** widen the lookback window and
  does **not** suppress the alarm — both would make it lie.
- **Triage-row width.** A `triage:` row still carries that suspect's whole skip-set, so a
  37-member workspace gives ~14 KB bodies. That width is `O(workspace)`, not `O(window)` —
  it is not the unbounded dimension, and capping it would add a second truncation site and
  a second disclosure for no bound improvement.
- **`failed_jobs` is uncapped.** Bounded by one run's job count (~84), not by the window.
- **`open_issue_exists()` still lists with `--limit 100`.** Same silent-truncation class as
  the render defect — if the open `selection-alarm` set ever exceeds 100, dedupe would
  quietly start minting duplicates. Not currently reachable (2 open) and out of scope here;
  noting it because it is the same failure mode, one layer over.
- It does not change which PRs are suspects, the dedupe keys, the fail-loud invariants, or
  the admission seam from #4982.

## Reviewer notes

Diff is **+300 / −6** across 2 files, no workflow change. The load-bearing questions:
1. Is **newest-first** the right end to keep, and is the intervening-coverage argument
   sound as a *prior*?
2. Is **20** the right bound?
3. `TestSuspectOrderIsLandingRecency` is the only thing standing between the body's

body:
# 通话态权限档跟随用户选择（ADR-053）

## 为什么推翻 D4 抬严

D4 的理由是「通话时用户手不在键盘、点不了确认」，效果却是「弹更多确认让他点」——
**理由和效果方向相反**。2026-07-29 真机实录：

| 时刻 | 动作 | 要不要确认 |
|---|---|---|
| 05:12:10 | 语音派活 | — |
| 05:12:23 | **用户挂断** | — |
| 05:13:45 | `ls -la ~` | 要 |
| 05:13:57 | `Write notes.md` | 要 |
| 05:14:04 | `ls -l notes.md` | 要 |

三张审批卡**全在挂断之后**弹出来，用户对着凭空出现的紫框点了三次，其中两次是只读的 `ls`。
安全上什么都没挡住（他不知道这是哪来的，只能全点允许），体验上把语音这条链堵死在第一步。

同时 D4 当初防的「无声改东西」这个前提，在发言人协议（#798）之后已经不成立。

## 决议

**档位跟随会话自己的选择。** 保障从「事前逐次点头」换成「事后可追溯」。

**唯一底线：`bypassPermissions` → `acceptEdits`。** 不是不信任用户，是语音独有的新风险——
ASR 会听错（同日实录「a.txt」听成「a点text」，落盘文件叫 `notes.md`）。文本模式下打错字
用户自己看得见，语音下看不见。同款钳制无人值守会话已有先例，照抄不自创。

## 连带清理

`readOnlyDenialError` 的通话专用文案分支已删。它当初存在是因为「请切换会话权限档」在钳档下
是假话；现在通话中还处在 readOnly 只可能是用户自己选的，那句恰恰是真话。留一条永远走不到、
内容已变假的分支，比没有更糟。

**通话态标记本身不废**——它还有第二个消费者（交互式工具收窄 `requiresUserPresence`），
那条仍必须罩住「挂断后 run 还在跑」的窗口，所以票据生命周期原样保留。

## 门：改写而非删除

旧门有 7 条钉的是被推翻的旧不变量，按房规改写成更本质的那条：

- 「通话态一律弹确认」→「**通话前后判定一模一样**」。判据仍打在真实审批决定上，
  不打在档位字段——档位从来不是放行的唯一闸门（`permissionClassifier` 的 W1 与档位无关，
  2026-07-26 那个洞就是这么漏的）。
- run 票据生命周期三条改成钉**标记**寿命（工具收窄仍靠它）。

**变异验证**：拆掉 `bypassPermissions` 底线 → 3 条红；退回旧的一律钳 `readOnly` → 6 条红。

## 验证

- `gates:local` **26/27**。permissions 93 passed、voice+orchestrator+security 356 passed、0 failed。
- 第 27 门（swarm e2e）本机红，**已确认与本改动无关**：在 `origin/main` 上复现同一条失败
  （同一个用例、同一句 `element(s) not found`）。根因是 `playwright.e2e.config.ts` 的
  `reuseExistingServer = !process.env.CI`——本机 8180 上跑着生产包，e2e 复用了它，
  于是拿旧 bundle 的 DOM 去断言。CI 里 `CI=true` 会自己起服务，不受影响。

## 已知缺口（后续工单已派）

本决议押在「事后可追溯」上，而这条链现在有个缺口：**发言人协议挂断即断**，
而语音派的 run 常常比通话活得久。挂断后才落地的活只剩会话里一张任务卡，用户得主动打开
才看得到。补法已立单（复用侧栏未读标记），**那条不落地，本决议就是真开了个洞**。

## What

Makes the documentation site **versioned** and ties deploys to releases.

- **mike** manages versioned docs on the `gh-pages` branch, and the Material theme shows a **version selector** (`extra.version.provider: mike`). Each released version keeps its own docs.
- The **Docs** workflow now runs on `release: published` (and `workflow_dispatch`), matching the Release workflow. On each release it runs `mike deploy <version> latest` + `mike set-default latest`.
- The versioned site is served through the **existing GitHub Pages "Actions" deployment** (no Pages source change, no Jekyll): the workflow assembles the `gh-pages` tree and injects the `CNAME` into the published artifact, so `drongo.proxyroot.com` keeps working.
- New **docs-check** workflow runs `mkdocs build --strict` on PRs that touch docs, so broken nav/links/refs still fail fast even though deploys only happen on release.

## Why

Requested: docs should be published on release, and should have versioning support.

## Verified locally
`mike deploy` + `set-default` produce the expected `gh-pages` layout (`versions.json`, per-version dirs, root redirect to `latest/`); `git archive` assembles a servable tree; `mkdocs build --strict` passes with the version provider.

## After merge
Versioning goes live on the next release. To activate it immediately (deploy the current docs as a version), run the Docs workflow via `workflow_dispatch` with `version=0.3.0`, `alias=latest`.

`AGENTS.md` is resident context on **every** model call an agent makes, so its size is a running
cost rather than a one-off — in the 2026-07-26 → 07-28 run, ~132k tokens of protocol across 4,885
coordinator calls. The `## WSL clusters and Slurm` section is 27 of its 150 lines: exhaustive,
safety-critical, and touched by essentially no issue in the M9/M10 backlog. Paid for on every call,
read on almost none.

This moves it to `docs/agents/hpc.md` and leaves a **fail-closed pointer** in its place: an agent
that has not read the page is not authorized to touch a cluster at all, and the "explicitly
authorizes the exact cluster, data, account, and resource ceiling" precondition stays in `AGENTS.md`
itself, so the authority rule is never one indirection away.

`AGENTS.md` 150 → **132** lines.

### It is a move, not a revision

The Slurm rules are safety rules and are not being renegotiated here. **All seven bullets are
byte-identical**, verified mechanically rather than by eye: each bullet from the pre-change

author: michalryskiewicz
body:
Third and last PR out of the security audit (H3). Independent of #5 and #6 except for one small README conflict, noted at the bottom.

## Why

Three decisions combined into one hole:

- `dek.store.ts` wrote the unwrapped data key to IndexedDB **permanently** — no expiry, no idle timeout, no re-prompt.
- `importDek` imported it as `extractable: true`, so anything in the origin could export the raw bytes.
- `decideAuthAccess` lets an offline device in without an identity.

So: take the laptop, turn off Wi-Fi, open the app — every financial record, no passphrase. The passphrase protected the first run on a device and nothing after it, which is not what "encrypted with a password we don't know" leads anyone to expect.

Per your call: **passphrase on every browser start**, plus a **30-minute idle lock**.

## What changed

**The key lives only in memory.** `DekStore` is gone; the data key exists in `VaultSession` and dies with the tab. `bootstrap()` can no longer return `unlocked` — every start begins locked. This is the change that costs you a passphrase entry per session and buys a stolen device being worth nothing.

**Dexie v3 deletes the `keys` table** rather than merely no longer writing to it. Every existing user has a key sitting on their disk right now; a release that only stopped persisting new ones would leave all of them there. There is a test for the upgrade path specifically.

**The key is non-extractable.** Nothing in the origin can read its bytes back out — an injected script can borrow it while the tab is open, but cannot carry it away or outlive the tab. Combined with #6's CSP, that is the pair of changes that actually make "the key never leaves the browser" true rather than aspirational.

That removes the only route from the key back to its raw material, so **`addKeyslot` / `replaceKeyslot` now take the secret that already opens the vault** instead of the unlocked key. The rule that falls out is the one worth having anyway: adding a way in costs proof that you already have one. Neither has a production caller yet (they are the passkey/rotation groundwork), so nothing else moved.

**`createIdleLock`, 30 minutes.** Idleness is judged **on the clock, not on a timer having fired** — a suspended laptop runs no timers and a background tab has them throttled, so a timer alone would let a machine wake hours later with the vault open. `check()` runs on `visibilitychange` and catches exactly that.

The lock drops the key straight from the session without going through the gate, so `resolveVaultGateStatus` re-checks the session on every render and brings `unlocked` back to `locked`. It deliberately does **not** interrupt `showing-recovery-code`: locking mid-setup would destroy the only copy of the recovery code that exists.

**The offline hole closes by itself.** With nothing cached, an offline start lands on the unlock screen, and the passphrase is verified by unwrapping the cached keyfile — pure crypto, no network. `decideAuthAccess` is therefore untouched: it was never the thing letting people in.

## Testing

`bun run test` — 264 passed, 5 skipped (pre-existing). `bun run lint`, `bun run typecheck` — clean.

New and rewritten, all red-first:
- `idle-lock.service.test.ts` (10) — locks at the timeout, not before; restarts on activity; **locks a machine that was asleep past the timeout on the next `check()`**; fires once however often it is asked; stops cleanly.
- `vault.service.test.ts` — the key is `extractable: false` and `exportKey` rejects; `addKeyslot` refuses a caller who cannot already open the vault.
- `vault-manager.test.ts` — a fresh start is always `locked`, however recently it ran; setup that fails to publish leaves the session locked.
- `keyfile-cache.store.test.ts` — **a key left by an older version is deleted on upgrade**; the cached keyfile survives it.
- `vault-gate-status.service.test.ts` — the gate follows a session locked behind its back, and leaves the recovery-code screen alone.

**Still manual before merge** — the timing and the browser side are not covered by any of that:

- [ ] Unlock, wait out 30 minutes idle, confirm the unlock screen returns and the app behind it is gone.
- [ ] Unlock, close the laptop, reopen after an hour, confirm it is locked on wake (this is the `check()` path a timer would miss).
- [ ] Confirm typing and scrolling actually postpone the lock — a false positive here is far more annoying than a late lock.
- [ ] Reload the tab mid-session and confirm the passphrase is asked for.
- [ ] **Upgrade path**: open the app as an existing user with a key already in IndexedDB, then check DevTools → Application → IndexedDB → `saldoo-vault` and confirm the `keys` store is gone.

## Cost, stated plainly

You will type the passphrase at least once per browser session, and 600k PBKDF2 iterations take roughly a second each time. That is the deal you picked, and it is the right one for a finance app, but it is a real daily cost and worth feeling before this merges rather than after.

## Conflict note

This touches `apps/frontend/src/database/sync/README.md` (the vault lifecycle table said "cached DEK", which is now wrong) — and #5 translates that same file to English. **Merge #5 first**; the resolution is to keep #5's English prose and apply this PR's content change to the lifecycle section. Nothing else overlaps.

author: pdcruze
body:
## Problem

The Triton prefill kernel computes element offsets in int32, which wraps negative once a tensor crosses 2^31 elements. Two paths are affected:

- **Q/out addressing** (`(row * n_q_heads + q_head) * head_dim + d`): overflows past 2^31 elements — e.g. 262,144 query rows at 32 heads × 256 head_dim. The q load then reads far out of bounds and the out store never lands.
- **Split-partial addressing** (`pid_lin * BLOCK_M * head_dim`): overflows when `programs * num_splits * BLOCK_M * head_dim` crosses 2^31, in both the prefill store and the combine-pass loads.

Separately, the auto-split heuristic can misbehave at large program counts: ceil-noise in the cost model can pick a high split count whose fp32 partial buffer runs to tens of GB (e.g. ~17 GB at 64k tokens × 32 heads) for negligible scheduling gain, causing OOM. We hit this evaluating a Gemma3-class model at long context.

## Fix

- Widen the row term (q/out) and `pid_lin` (partials) to int64 in `_paged_attn_prefill_kernel` and `_paged_attn_prefill_combine_kernel`.
- Clamp the auto-picked `num_splits` so the partial buffer stays under 128 MB, and guard the heuristic against `programs == 0`.

## Tests

`tests/test_triton_paged_overflow.py` crosses the 2^31 element-offset boundary in both paths and checks exact expected values, using a NaN sentinel in `out` so a wrapped store is detected. Both tests were verified to fail against the previous kernel and pass with the fix. Note for CI: crossing 2^31 elements inherently requires large allocations, so the tests need ~10–11 GiB of free VRAM and skip below that. A third small test covers the `programs == 0` guard.

author: milkclouds
body:
## Summary

Adds a harness-wide way to run a benchmark without a GPU, so a single-GPU host can give the device to the policy and render the simulator on the CPU.

Today this is impossible. CUDA compute and GPU rendering readback on the same device abort nondeterministically in the NVIDIA driver — an observed controlled A/B was 6/6 stable when split across devices vs 4/4 aborting when co-tenant — and there is no way to start a benchmark container without a GPU at all.

```bash
vla-eval run --config configs/benchmarks/libero/all.yaml --render cpu
```

## Design

- **Surface**: top-level `render: gpu|cpu` (default `gpu`) plus CLI `--render`, resolved in `cmd_run` like `--server-url`. Run-level, because the renderer binds at the first simulator import and cannot be re-bound in-process. Top-level rather than under `docker:` so `--no-docker` runs behave the same.
- **Capability**: `Benchmark.render_backends` declares support and `Benchmark.configure_render(mode)` applies it, returning the env it set. The default is gpu-only and raises on `cpu`, so an unmigrated or new benchmark fails fast instead of crashing mid-run.
- **Application point**: `Orchestrator._run_benchmark_inner`, after `resolve_import_string` and before construction — no import-time global mutation. `src/vla_eval/render.py` holds the shared per-family env so an adapter's override is one line.
- **Unsupported combinations** fail host-side before the docker pull, naming the benchmarks. Falling back to GPU would reinstate the crash the user is avoiding.
- **GPU flags**: `render: cpu` emits no `--gpus` and sets `NVIDIA_VISIBLE_DEVICES=void`. `docker.gpus: "none"` becomes a valid spec; previously it produced the broken flag `--gpus device=none`, so there was no way to express "no GPU" at all.

Conflicts between the two knobs are resolved in one place, `check_gpu_spec_conflict`, shared by `run` and the smoke path so they cannot drift:

| | outcome |
|---|---|
| `--render cpu` + YAML `gpus:` | CLI wins, forced to `none` |
| YAML `render: cpu` + YAML `gpus:` | rejected, the config contradicts itself |
| `--render cpu` + `--gpus` | rejected, same precedence so neither outranks |
| `gpus: none` + `render: gpu` | rejected, the simulator needs a device |

**Provenance**: the requested mode and the applied env are recorded in benchmark metadata and flow into the merge aggregate. `upsert_eval_metadata` is first-writer-wins, so under sharding a differing second write now sets `render.divergent` and logs both values rather than silently reporting one shard's answer for every episode. RoboMME's `ROBOMME_USE_LAVAPIPE=auto` probes per process, which is a real mechanism for shards to disagree.

**Smoke hardening**: episode failures are isolated by design, so a run where *every* episode errored still exits 0 and writes an aggregate — and `vla-eval test` used to report that as a pass. It now fails when the aggregate contains errored episodes, naming the first error. This is not hypothetical: it is exactly how two of this PR's own support claims initially passed while being broken (below).

## Migration

Zero-touch for every benchmark via the base default. Support was decided by measuring
each image with no GPU attached, not by the simulator's name — see the table in
[docs/render-backends.md](docs/render-backends.md). Every row is a measurement; none is
guessed.

Declared, with the per-family switch:

- **LIBERO** (and Pro/Plus/Mem by inheritance), **RoboCasa**, **RoboCasa365**,
  **RoboCerebra**, **VLABench**, **MolmoSpaces-Bench**: MuJoCo → OSMesa.
- **MolmoSpaces-Bench** additionally needs a stub for the macOS-only `mujoco.cgl`
  module: molmo_spaces' renderer calls its lock/unlock helpers on exactly the GPU-less
  path (with CUDA available it takes its own EGL class), and that module hard-dlopens
  the macOS OpenGL framework.
- **DuoBench**: *not* OSMesa — its rcs camera stack bootstraps a real EGL context
  regardless of `MUJOCO_GL` (`rcs.sim.egl_bootstrap`), so cpu keeps EGL and pins
  `MUJOCO_EGL_DEVICE_ID` to the Mesa software rasterizer, the only EGL device in a
  GPU-less container.
- **Kinetix**: JAX, no GL; `JAX_PLATFORMS=cpu` is the whole switch. The adapter also
  needed migrating to the image's `make_kinetix_env` API — as shipped, 0.4.0's
  adapter/image pair could not construct an env on *either* backend
  (`make_kinetix_env_from_name` no longer exists), which had gone unnoticed for
  exactly the smoke-blindness reason above.
- **RoboMME**: SAPIEN 3.0.3 → lavapipe.
- **CALVIN**: PyBullet → TinyRenderer. The EGL plugin hard-exits the process with no
  GPU ("failed to EGL with glad"), so cpu refuses the plugin and renders with
  PyBullet's built-in software rasterizer — frames are close to, but not
  pixel-identical with, the GPU path's.

Not declared, with the measured reason:

- **SimplerEnv, ManiSkill2, RoboTwin, MIKASA-Robo**: their SAPIEN builds (2.2.2 /
  3.0.0b1) require the Vulkan device extension `VK_KHR_external_semaphore_fd` at
  `vkCreateDevice` — before any shader or scene configuration — and Mesa's lavapipe
  does not implement it. Reproduced identically against Mesa 23.2 (the images') and
  Mesa 25.0, so a Mesa bump does not close the gap; SAPIEN 3.0.3 dropped the hard
  requirement, which is why RoboMME works. These need newer SAPIEN builds, not harness
  work.
- **BEHAVIOR-1K**: Isaac Sim dumps core during extension startup with no GPU.
- **RoboDojo**: Isaac reports `ERROR_INCOMPATIBLE_DRIVER` / "Failed to create any GPU
  devices"; the RTX renderer has no software path.

One pre-existing breakage surfaced by the measurements and left for its own fix:
**RLBench** cannot run at all — the front camera returns all-black frames with and
without a GPU, the pinned RLBench 1.1.0 predates the adapter's imports
(`rlbench.action_modes.action_mode` does not exist at that tag), and
`natsort`/`pyquaternion` are missing from its env. Unlike Kinetix this needs an image
rebuild, not an adapter change.

Corrections to what the code previously asserted, all from measuring rather than
reading: MolmoSpaces-Bench was excluded on the grounds that it "renders through
AI2-THOR", but `ai2thor` is not installed in its image at all. `configs/README.md`
labelled VLABench as SAPIEN when it is dm_control/MuJoCo — and RoboMME and MIKASA-Robo
as MuJoCo when both are SAPIEN.

## Validation

The published images bake the harness at build time, so a plain smoke run exercises the
old in-container code and silently skips `configure_render`. Every run below therefore
mounts this branch's src over the image's copy — now first-class as
`vla-eval test --dev`, mirroring `vla-eval run --dev` — and three things were checked
inside the merge aggregate, not just the exit status: the episode ran (`steps` > 0),
no episode errored, and the recorded provenance shows the CPU backend actually engaged
(`applied_env`).

That check is what caught DuoBench and MolmoSpaces-Bench "passing" in 7s with every
episode errored, and it is now built into `vla-eval test` itself.

| Benchmark | `--render cpu`, no GPU attached | applied_env observed |
|---|---|---|
| LIBERO | pass, 50 steps | OSMesa |
| LIBERO-Pro | pass, 50 steps | OSMesa |
| LIBERO-Plus | pass, 50 steps | OSMesa |
| LIBERO-Mem | pass, 50 steps | OSMesa |
| RoboCasa | pass, 5 steps (config cap) | OSMesa |
| RoboCasa365 | pass, 8 steps | OSMesa |
| RoboCerebra | pass, 50 steps | OSMesa |
| DuoBench | pass, 50 steps | EGL + `MUJOCO_EGL_DEVICE_ID=0` |
| VLABench | pass, 50 steps | OSMesa |
| MolmoSpaces-Bench | pass, 50 steps | OSMesa |
| RoboMME (4 suites) | pass, 1 step each (config cap) | lavapipe |
| CALVIN | pass, 50 steps | TinyRenderer via `CALVIN_USE_EGL=0` |
| Kinetix | pass, 28 steps | JAX cpu (`JAX_PLATFORMS=cpu`) |

GPU control runs (same mounted code, GPU attached, no `--render`) pass for DuoBench,
MolmoSpaces-Bench and Kinetix — 28 steps on both Kinetix backends, matching exactly, as
the deterministic seeding intends — so the cpu-path changes did not disturb the GPU pat

## Summary
This PR significantly optimizes the trip direction chevron layer rendering performance by implementing two key strategies: caching simplified polyline geometry per zoom level and tracking the screen area covered by drawn chevrons to avoid unnecessary line re-stroking.

## Key Changes

### Chevron Layer Optimization (`trip_direction_chevron_layer.dart`)
- **Geometry Caching**: Added `_ProjectedPath.simplified()` method that caches the thinned point list per zoom level, allowing panning to reuse simplified geometry instead of re-projecting every point each frame
- **Region Tracking**: Introduced `_ChevronRegion` class using a grid-based cell system to track where chevrons have been drawn on screen, enabling selective re-stroking of only trips that overlap with chevron areas
- **Improved Decimation**: Replaced per-frame point decimation with zoom-level-based simplification tolerance calculation (`_planarToleranceSq`), ensuring consistent visual quality across fractional zooms
- **Bounds Calculation**: Added `_chevronReach` constant and proper bounding box tracking for drawn chevrons to accurately determine which trips need re-stroking
- **Return Value Changes**: Modified `_drawPolylineWorld` to return the screen area covered by chevrons (or null) instead of a boolean, enabling proper region tracking

### Settings UI Refactoring (`settings_page.dart`)
- Reorganized debug settings into a dedicated `_buildDebugSection` method for better code organization
- Moved debug options under a separate "Debug" section header when in debug mode
- Unified debug icon usage across all debug settings

### Map Zoom Limits (`map_page.dart`)
- Added explicit `minZoom: 0` and `maxZoom: 22` to `MapOptions` to prevent crashes from invalid zoom values during rapid pinch gestures
- Added detailed comment explaining the issue and solution

### Changelog Updates
- Added fix entry documenting the map zoom limit crash prevention across all language variants (English, French, Japanese, Tagalog)

### Platform Utils (`platform_utils.dart`)
- Added `debug` icon constant to `AdaptiveIcons` class

## Implementation Details
- The grid-based `_ChevronRegion` uses 32-pixel cells to balance memory usage and accuracy
- Simplification tolerance is derived at the next whole zoom level to ensure cached lists are never coarser than per-frame decimation
- The first and last points are always preserved during simplification to maintain path continuity from departure to arrival
- Conservative cell marking ensures the region test may request unnecessary re-strokes but never skips required ones

body:
## What & why (audit §4)

### Game removal 500'd on a foreign key
`score→game`, `team→game`, and `game_result→game` were all `NO ACTION`, so deleting a game that had *any* play data was refused by Postgres → 500. All three are now `ON DELETE CASCADE` (entities + migration), so removing a game cleanly drops its scores, teams, and result record.

### Removal guard was stale
`removeGameFromSession` / `updateSessionGames` only blocked `IN_PROGRESS`. Under the new state machine a game mid-play can also be `ROUND_IN_PROGRESS` / `ROUND_ENDED` / `PAUSED` — those were removable, which could nuke a game out from under live players. Now all mid-play states are blocked; only not-started or finished games can be removed.

### Adding the same game twice
`addGamesToSession` now de-duplicates the incoming ids and skips libraries already present in the session (400 if nothing new remains), so a game can't be double-added server-side (the FE filter that should prevent this is fixed in the frontend PR).

## Tests
New e2e: submit a score to the seeded active game, then `DELETE /games/:id` → **204** and the game is gone (previously a 500). **348 unit / 46 e2e** green. Migration hand-reviewed (stripped TypeORM's unrelated invite-FK churn) and verified drift-free.

## Deploy
BE-only; migration runs on boot (three `ALTER TABLE … FK … ON DELETE CASCADE`).

## Summary

- Remove `strava` from `LEGACY_CALLBACK_CONNECTOR_REFS` now that the Strava OAuth app accepts the App callback URL.
- Extend the connectors-page `it.each` so Strava is covered by the same assertion as every other App-callback connector.

## User impact

Connecting Strava now completes OAuth through the dedicated App callback page at `/connectors/strava/callback` instead of `<web>/api/connectors/strava/callback`, matching the redirect URI configured on the Strava side.

## Implementation notes

- Since #23392 inverted this module, the set is a denylist and `isConnectorAppOauthCallbackEnabled` returns `!has(ref)`. Enabling a connector therefore means deleting its line, not adding one.
- The same helper gates both sides — `turbo/apps/api/src/signals/routes/connector-oauth-origin.ts` (authoritative for `redirect_uri`) and `turbo/apps/platform/src/signals/zero-page/settings/connectors.ts` (decides whether to send `callbackTarget: "app"`) — so one deletion moves the whole flow.
- Strava is `auth-code` with `callbackOrigin: "web"` in `provider-capabilities.ts`, so it takes the App callback path once un-denylisted. #23392 removed the `callbackOrigin === "web"` condition from the API gate, which now only checks `callbackTarget === "app" && isConnectorAppOauthCallbackEnabled(ref)`.
- Rollout is safe in both cross-version pairings. New frontend + old backend: the frontend sends `callbackTarget: "app"`, the old backend still has `strava` denylisted and returns the legacy URL, so the flow completes over the old path. Old frontend + new backend: no `callbackTarget` is sent, so the legacy path is used. The API independently re-checks its own copy of the list and owns the `redirect_uri`, so no unregistered redirect can reach the provider mid-rollout.

## Verification

- `zero-connectors-page.test.tsx` asserts `body.callbackTarget === "app"` and the resulting auth-window navigation per connector, so this row fails if `strava` is still denylisted — the change is locked in rather than merely accompanied by a test.
- Existing API coverage of the mechanism is unchanged: `uses App callbacks by default outside the legacy callback list` and `keeps denylisted API-origin callbacks on the API`. No per-ref API test is added; the additions here are data, not new mechanism.
- Per the repo's PR preference, full local vitest was not run; the PR pipeline covers it.

## Remaining connectors

Current best score: 1.46824739821125. This PR's own benchmark run scores the head commit;
the PR is merged automatically if the submission is accepted, and closed with the result otherwise.

---

**Submitter note**

Model: Poolside Laguna XS 2.1 NVFP4

# Two bit-exact stacked wins: the QKV projection's missing LOADS-ONLY unroll, and the NOVOL staging lever promoted to default

**What this changes, in two lines:**

```
Sources/MLXFastModel/LagunaRuntimeModel.swift  — depth-2 block unroll in the
   fused norm+QKV+gate projection (new DARKBLOOM_QKV_UNROLL, default 2)
Vendor/.../backend/metal/quantized.cpp          — darkbloom_stage_novol()
   defaults ON (fc 207) instead of opt-in
```

Both are scheduling/load-order changes with no arithmetic reassociation.
Measured separately, both positive, and they touch different phases (decode
GEMV vs prefill staging), so they stack.

---

## 1. The fused QKV projection never got the unroll its sibling has

`lagunaGatedOutputProjectionSource` carries a documented, promoted depth-2
block unroll behind `DARKBLOOM_L5_UNROLL`, with an explicit **LOADS ONLY**
discipline in its comment: hoist consecutive blocks' loads, keep one
accumulator per row stepped in strict `(block, i)` order, never introduce
per-step partial sums (which would regroup the FP32 chain into a tree, pass
every local check, and fail the hidden exact-token gate).

`lagunaFusedQKVProjectionSource` — the *larger* of the two attention GEMVs —
never received it. Its block loop was still the plain one-block-at-a-time
form. That kernel is the single biggest consumer on the decode step in my
profiling: at h=64 it moves 42.2 MB/token-layer across 30 sliding layers, and
in a shape-matched micro-bench it ran at 519-546 GB/s while a stock MLX
matmul over the same byte volume on the same machine ran at 599-656 GB/s.

**The change:** identical structure to the promoted L5 unroll. `blocks` is
`in_vec_size / block_width` = 2048/128 = 16, divisible by 1/2/4/8, so no
depth needs a tail loop and depth 1 re-emits the pre-patch loop verbatim —
a true ablation control, not an approximation of one.

**Exactness:** `result[row]` remains ONE accumulator per row, stepped block 0
products then block 1 products into the same register, in the same `i` order.
Only the *loads* are hoisted. No partial sums, no tree, no reassociation, and
the reduction, the BF16 rounding, and the write are untouched.

**Measurement** (M5 Max, 128 GB, quiescent, external cooling; in-process
driver over the runtime worker's own protocol, 400 steady decode steps per
arm, median of arm; 6 arms interleaved A-B-B-A-A-B so drift cancels):

```
unroll 2 (this patch) : 8.661  8.672  8.681   mean 8.671 ms
unroll 1 (control)    : 8.696  8.695  8.729   mean 8.707 ms
                                              -0.41% decode
```

Every treated arm is faster than every control arm — zero overlap between the
distributions.

**Depth sweep** (8 arms, palindromic order, same rig), because the honest
question is whether deeper is better:

```
   QKV=2, L5=2 (shipped here)   8.683 ms    +0.00%   <- optimum
   QKV=2, L5=4                  8.901 ms    +2.51%
   QKV=4, L5=2                  8.973 ms    +3.33%
   QKV=4, L5=4                  9.189 ms    +5.83%
```

Depth 4 regresses on both kernels — register pressure, consistent with the
`notes/46` occupancy framing. Depth 2 is the optimum for the QKV kernel and
independently re-confirms the promoted L5 default of 2. I am shipping the
knob (1/2/4/8) so the next person can re-sweep it on a different tree without
rebuilding the reasoning.

## 2. DARKBLOOM_STAGE_NOVOL promoted from opt-in to default

`quantized.cpp` documents four staging levers behind function constants
(WIDEST 204 / WIDELD 205 / RUNBAR 206 / NOVOL 207), all opt-in. NOVOL drops a
vestigial `volatile` in the k-loop — a pure scheduling change, selected as a
distinct pipeline variant, resolved once per process.

Measured with gated `--local-iterate` runs, 4 arms interleaved:

```
NOVOL on  : prefill 568.4, 564.6 us   mean 566.5   -1.77% prefill
NOVOL off : prefill 570.9, 582.5 us   mean 576.7
            decode +0.18% (flat, inside noise)
```

Its three siblings re-measured NEGATIVE on this tree and stay opt-in, which
is why this submission promotes only NOVOL:

```
WIDEST+WIDELD+RUNBAR+NOVOL together : prefill +1.1%, decode +1.8%  (worse)
NOVOL+RUNBAR                        : prefill +3.6% vs NOVOL alone (worse)
```

## Combined expectation

`score = decode_speedup^0.75 * prefill_speedup^0.25`, so -0.41% decode and
-1.77% prefill predict roughly +0.31% + +0.44% ≈ **+0.75%** over the tree
these were measured against (`5531848`). Modest, honest, and both halves are
bit-exact rather than approximations traded against the gate.

## Verification

- `swift test --force-resolved-versions`: 446 tests, 6 suites, all pass.
- Public drift tripwire: `passed: true`, 64/64 checked steps, no failing step.
- `./benchmark.sh --local-submit`: full gated run, all checked tokens
  accepted.
- Both changes carry same-binary ablation switches (`DARKBLOOM_QKV_UNROLL=1`,
  `DARKBLOOM_STAGE_NOVOL=0`) that restore the previous behavior verbatim, so
  either can be A/B'd or reverted without a rebuild.

## Things I measured and did NOT ship (so nobody re-derives them)

Everything below was tested on this box tonight against the same rig and
rejected on evidence:

- **Extending the promoted GQA head-pairing from 2 heads to 4** (sliding
  layers only, gqa_factor 8 divides evenly, correctness green): **+2.60%
  slower** on 6 interleaved arms. The pairing submission's own comment says
  "two heads are deliberately conservative" — that is a measured frontier,
  not headroom. Register state per threadgroup outgrows the K/V reread saving.
- **Order-safe weight repacking** for the QKV bank (relaying weights at load
  time so each lane's two block-chunks are contiguous 16B, preserving exact
  accumulation order): 485-544 GB/s, *worse* than the production shape. Wide
  contiguous weight loads are not the mechanism.
- **NAX scheduling transforms applied to the sites the recent promotions left
  alone** (gemm_nax mainloop, fp_qmm_t/n: NO_UNROLL->UNROLL plus volatile
  removal, the same edit that worked in fp_quantized_nax's gather kernels):
  **prefill +38%, decode +8%**. Those sites were left alone for a reason.
- **`MLX_MAX_OPS_PER_BUFFER` 50 vs 200**: -0.47%, inside a 1.2-3.2%
  within-arm noise band at n=2. Inconclusive, not shipped.
- **fp4 (nvfp4 gs16) coarse pass for the lm_head pruner**: simulated offline
  against 136 real decode hidden states with a bit-faithful quantizer replica
  before writing any Metal — the certified candidate set explodes (p50 27k of
  100k rows), and the extra exact-pass bytes exceed the coarse saving. This
  is presumably why the shipped pruner stops at mxfp8.
- **Collapsing the pruner's post-coarse tail from six dispatches to two**
  (single-threadgroup threshold reduction + inline candidacy in the exact
  pass, bit-exact, correctness green): -0.10%, i.e. null. The pipelined
  stream already hides small dispatch latency; the dispatch-count family is
  not where the remaining time is.
- **Re-validating three existing fusions by ablation** (this tree is
  well-tuned and I wanted to know if any promotion had rotted): MoE decode
  fusions are worth **+8.10%**, fused QKV projection **+1.95%**, fused
  residual+RMS+router **+1.79%**. All three earn their place.

author: wallstreethyena
body:
fix(guards): three assertions could not fail — and a meta-guard so it can't recur

AGENTS.md §4: "A check that cannot fail is worse than no check, because it
launders an unknown into a green." Three were live inside the 173-guard suite,
all shaped ok(!/regex/.test(x) || true, "..."), all NEGATIVE assertions.

Per guard, bypass deleted FIRST and the result reported before anything was
fixed:

  test-device-id.mjs:19          -> RED
  test-ranking-editorial.mjs:15  -> green
  test-experiment.mjs:122        -> green (and had an empty message)

Two of the three passed the moment the bypass was removed. The `|| true` was
never needed on either — added defensively, never revisited. That is the whole
argument for the meta-guard: nobody goes back.

THE ONE THAT WAS RED, AND WHY IT MATTERED

test-device-id.mjs sits between two live privacy checks — Do-Not-Track /
wf_optout, and session-only ids for opted-out users. The line after it asserts
only that a COMMENT about the policy exists. So the suite was verifying that our
privacy PROMISE is written down while the check that it is HONOURED was switched
off.

Root cause: the old regex text-searched app/home.js for
Flash|ETag|canvas|IndexedDB|CacheStorage|evercookie|fingerprint — and
app/home.js:436-437 is the POLICY COMMENT promising we do none of them. The
comment matched itself. A text search cannot tell a promise from a practice.

Fixed by expressing the real property: no CALL to a resurrection or
fingerprinting API, scanned over source with comments AND string literals
stripped, so the policy statement can keep naming what it forbids. Detects
IndexedDB.open, CacheStorage.open, canvas getContext->toDataURL, navigator.plugins,
RTCPeerConnection, AudioContext fingerprinting — and names which one it found.

RED-PROVEN: injecting `indexedDB.open("wf_resurrect")` into deviceId() turns it
red with "(found: IndexedDB.open())"; removing it turns it green. It could not
do that before. A third assertion proves the comment-stripper works, so the
check cannot silently go vacuous if the stripper regexes ever break.

THE META-GUARD — scripts/check-guards-can-fail.mjs (in guards.txt, same commit)

Fails on any ok(...) with a tautological `|| true` / `|| 1`, a literal
ok(true, ...), or an empty failure message. 189 guard files scanned, currently
clean. Red-proven on both shapes.

Two things it taught me while I wrote it, both worth recording:

1. It flagged ITSELF — its detection patterns live in its own regexes and error
   strings. Stripping string literals would not help, since the patterns are
   inside regex literals. Self-exclusion is the honest fix, and its own
   assertions are exercised by the red-prove rather than by itself.

2. First run reported 10 empty-message findings across 9 files. All FALSE
   POSITIVES: /,\s*""\s*\)/ matches any inner `.replace(x, "")` on the same
   line. That is the §4(c) shape — the check ran correctly and answered a
   different question. It now parses the ok(...) call with balanced parens and
   inspects the LAST top-level argument. Had I trusted the first run I would
   have "fixed" nine healthy files.

VERIFIED
  node scripts/run-guards.mjs -> 174/174, EXIT=0
  npm run check:jsx           -> EXIT=0
  npx next build              -> EXIT=0, four landing routes still SSG

`location` fields and every real attempt named the affected symbol only in
prose. That is a real, pre-existing grader defect (present since the
grader's original commit, not introduced by #53 or by this branch's own
relevance-guard commit) - fixed here, then used to re-grade both the
post-#53 attempts already captured and a fresh pre-#53 (commit `8e4fdbd`,
#52's merge) run of the same two cases, for a genuine apples-to-apples
comparison.

- `review-suite/scripts/evals/grader.py`: a referred-path relevance guard
  (`referred_relevant_root_cause_ids`, `combined_recall` on `grade()`) so a
  referred candidate only counts toward the preregistered v2 gate's
  alternative pass path when it concretely names the actual surface, plus a
  real fix (`surface_named_in_prose`) recognizing a symbol named only in a
  finding's prose - constrained by, and verified against, this repository's
  own `probe.partial-claim-wrong-surface` calibration boundary. `report.py`
  surfaces both at the per-case level. `GRADER_VERSION` `1.0` -> `1.1`
  (behavioral, versioned accordingly; every corpus/calibration file's
  declared version bumped to match).
- `review-suite/scripts/evals/regrade.py` (new) + `just
  regrade-review-suite`: re-grade already-captured raw attempts with the
  current grader, no new executor calls, no new spend.
- `review-suite/evals/v2/` (new files only - nothing under
  `baseline/v1/`, `gate-manifest.json`, `DECISION-RECORD.md`,
  `FAILURE-TAXONOMY.md`, or `audits/` was touched):
  - `s1-rescore-frozen-configuration.json` - the re-score configuration,

  - `s1-correctness-orchestrator.report.json` - post-#53, 35 attempts,
    re-graded with the fixed grader.
  - `pre53-s1-correctness-orchestrator-2case.report.json` - a fresh 10
    attempts pre-#53, graded with the same fixed grader.
  - `GRADER-1.1-COMPARABILITY.md` - what changed and why a grader-version
    change is a new, non-comparable stratum (extending the existing
    runtime/model-change rule).
  - `s1-rescore-pre-post-comparison.md` - the four-number comparison,
    non-regression floor check, spend, and a recommendation (not a
    decision) for the repository owner.

## Result

author: amaadmartin
body:
Please ensure you have read the contribution guide before creating a pull request.

### Link to Issue or Description of Change

1. Link to an existing issue (if applicable):

_No existing issue._

2. Or, if no issue exists, describe the change:

**Problem**: ADK reserves two function-call names for human-in-the-loop (HITL) pauses: `adk_request_credential` (the agent needs end-user credentials before a tool can run) and `adk_request_confirmation` (the agent needs the user to approve a tool call). An application embedding ADK has to recognise these in the event stream to render the right UI and to send the matching function _response_ back.

Only one of the two is reachable from the published package. `REQUEST_CONFIRMATION_FUNCTION_CALL_NAME` is exported from `@google/adk`, but `REQUEST_EUC_FUNCTION_CALL_NAME` is not: `core/src/common.ts` re-exports exactly three names from `./agents/functions.js` and neither constant, and there is no wildcard re-export of that module anywhere in `common.ts` or `index.ts`. So a consumer writing an auth/EUC HITL loop has to hardcode the string literal `'adk_request_credential'`, which silently rots if the reserved name is ever changed, while the confirmation half of the very same loop gets to use an imported constant.

**Solution**: Add `REQUEST_EUC_FUNCTION_CALL_NAME` to the existing `export {...} from './agents/functions.js';` block in `core/src/common.ts`, making the pair symmetric on the public surface:

```ts
import {REQUEST_EUC_FUNCTION_CALL_NAME} from '@google/adk';

if (part.functionCall?.name === REQUEST_EUC_FUNCTION_CALL_NAME) {
  // Surface the auth prompt, then reply with a functionResponse of the
  // same name carrying the credential.
}
```

This is purely additive and has no runtime behaviour change — the constant is already declared and already used internally; this only widens what the entry point exposes. Since `common.ts` already re-exports from `./agents/functions.js`, no new module edge is introduced into the barrel's import graph.

Notes on deliberate scope limits:

- The change extends the **existing** export block rather than adding a second `export ... from './agents/functions.js'` statement.
- `REQUEST_CONFIRMATION_FUNCTION_CALL_NAME` is deliberately **not** added to this block. That identifier is declared twice in the repo (`core/src/agents/functions.ts` and `core/src/plugins/security_plugin.ts`), and `common.ts` already re-exports the `security_plugin.js` one; re-exporting it from a second module here would be a TS2308 duplicate-export error. Consolidating that duplicate declaration is a real wart but is left for a separate change.
- Existing in-repo call sites that hardcode the literal are intentionally left untouched to keep this diff to the single additive export.

Diff is 2 files, +8 lines: `core/src/common.ts` (+1) and `core/test/agents/functions_test.ts` (+7).

### Testing Plan

Please describe the tests that you ran to verify your changes. This is required for all PRs that are not small documentation or typo fixes.

Unit Tests:
[x] I have added or updated unit tests for my change.
[x] All unit tests pass locally.

Added to `core/test/agents/functions_test.ts`:

```ts
describe('REQUEST_EUC_FUNCTION_CALL_NAME', () => {
  it('is exported from the public package entry point', () => {
    expect(REQUEST_EUC_FUNCTION_CALL_NAME).toBe('adk_request_credential');
  });
});
```

The import is the load-bearing half: the symbol is imported from `'@google/adk'` (not via a relative path), so the test exercises the barrel. The `toBe` additionally pins the wire value, which is matched against `functionCall.name` / `functionResponse.name` and is shared with adk-python.

```
$ npx vitest run --project unit:core core/test/agents/functions_test.ts
 Test Files  1 passed (1)
      Tests  28 passed (28)
```

**Negative control** — I verified the assertion is not vacuous by temporarily deleting the new line from `core/src/common.ts` and re-running:

```
 × REQUEST_EUC_FUNCTION_CALL_NAME > is exported from the public package entry point
   AssertionError: expected undefined to be 'adk_request_credential'
 Tests  1 failed | 27 passed (28)
```

Worth recording: the other 27 tests still passed. Under Vite's TS transform a missing named import resolves to `undefined` rather than raising an ESM link error, so the bare `import` is _not_ self-enforcing — this assertion is what actually guards the export under the runner. The line was restored before committing.

Manual End-to-End (E2E) Tests:
Please provide instructions on how to manually test your changes, including any necessary setup or configuration.

The unit test resolves `@google/adk` through the vitest alias to `core/src`, so I additionally verified the real built artifacts, with no mocks and no aliasing:

```

npm run build

# Type surface:
grep -n "REQUEST_EUC_FUNCTION_CALL_NAME" core/dist/types/common.d.ts

# ESM runtime:

# CJS runtime:
node --input-type=commonjs -e "console.log(require('./core/dist/cjs/index.js').REQUEST_EUC_FUNCTION_CALL_NAME);"
```

Both runtimes print `adk_request_credential`, and the constant appears in the generated `common.d.ts`.

This pull request introduces several improvements and refactorings across the codebase, focusing on graph processing, rendering performance, and experiment reproducibility. The most important changes include a new script for generating test graphs, significant optimizations to rendering large graphs, improved spectral coordinate computation, and updates to experiment configurations for better control and reproducibility.

**New utilities and experiment reproducibility:**
* Added a new script `generate_test_graph.py` that samples connected subgraphs from ConceptNet with configurable edge weights and confidence values, supporting multiple weighting strategies for more controlled and reproducible experiments.
* Updated experiment configuration in `experiment.metta` to use new data sources and static imports, ensuring experiments use the intended test graphs and data. 

**Rendering and visualization improvements:**
* Refactored the `render.py` animation function to use vectorized scatter plotting for rendering large graphs, limiting the number of rendered and labeled nodes for performance and clarity, and dynamically scaling node sizes by importance. 
* Cleaned up imports and removed unnecessary blank lines in `render.py` for improved readability. 

**Graph computation and core logic:**
* Improved the spectral coordinate calculation in `graph.py` by switching to the LOBPCG algorithm for better performance and stability on large sparse Laplacians, and added diagonal preconditioning. 
* Refactored the main simulation logic in `connection.py` to ensure that STI values are generated or loaded before graph data is processed, and streamlined the flow for both animated and non-animated runs.

Thresholds look sensible. Script can be rerun against real child data as the app scales.

## 概述

实现一个端到端、可验证的自动代码评审 Agent 原型，交付目录为：

```text
examples/skills_code_review_agent/
```

输入支持 unified diff / PR patch、指定文件列表、Git 工作区变更和内置 fixture。系统通过 `code-review` Skill 加载受控规则脚本，经 Filter 前置治理后在 SDK workspace sandbox 中执行检查；随后将问题按严重级别、文件、行号、证据和修复建议结构化输出，并把任务、Filter 决策、沙箱运行、finding、报告与指标写入 SQLite。

核心取舍是“确定性规则负责检出，LLM 仅做受限文本增强”：

- 正则 + Python AST 规则保证 fake model / dry-run 下仍可复现、可测试；
- LLM 只能增强 summary、recommendation 和人工复核提示；
- LLM 不得增删 finding，也不得修改 identity、severity、confidence、bucket 或去重结果；
- 无 API Key 时可使用 dry-run / fake model 完整验证解析、Filter、沙箱和落库链路。

## 架构

```text
diff / files / Git workspace / fixture
  → 输入校验与受控 staging
  → code-review Skill：diff 解析 + 确定性规则
  → Filter 前置治理（DENY / NEEDS_HUMAN_REVIEW 不进沙箱）
  → SDK workspace sandbox
       - Container：生产默认，验证 network_mode=none
       - Local：仅显式开发 fallback
       - Cube：无可验证无出口网络证明时默认拒绝
  → finding 去重与四桶路由
       - dedup key: (file, line, category)
       - findings / needs_human_review / suppressed / warnings
  → 三层脱敏与最终出口扫描
  → canonical review_report.json
       ├── review_report.md
       ├── SQLite 五张 cr_* 业务表
       └── metrics / telemetry / audit summary
```

Agent 入口实际复用 SDK `LlmAgent + SkillToolSet`：

```text
user-query
  → skill_load("code-review")
  → 受控 skill_run(request_id)
  → ReviewPipeline.run()
```

CLI、Agent、dry-run 和测试共用同一个 `ReviewPipeline`，不复制规则或报告逻辑。

## 核心能力

- **code-review Skill**：包含 SKILL.md、6 类规则文档、manifest 和隔离脚本。
- **规则覆盖**：安全风险、敏感信息、异步错误、资源泄漏、数据库生命周期、测试缺失。
- **四类输入**：`--diff-file`、`--repo-path`、`--files`、`--fixture`，互斥校验。
- **结构化 finding**：severity、category、file、line、title、evidence、recommendation、confidence、source。
- **SQLite 持久化**：`cr_review_task`、`cr_sandbox_run`、`cr_filter_event`、`cr_finding`、`cr_report`；支持按 task id 查询完整 bundle。
- **安全边界**：manifest allowlist、超时、单次/总输出上限、环境变量白名单、网络拒绝、失败即数据、无宿主回退。
- **脱敏闭环**：检测与脱敏共享规则源，原始 diff、代码、环境变量、明文凭据不会进入 LLM、日志、Telemetry、报告或数据库。
- **报告**：canonical JSON schema 校验后原子写入，再由同一对象确定性渲染 Markdown。

## 验收对照（issue #92）

| # | 验收项 | 状态 | 当前证据 |
|---|---|---|---|

author: linyiru
body:
## The bug (production, silent)

A streamed inbound reply (Slack \`respondTo\` + \`stream: true\`) is rendered by the **webhook worker** consuming the DO's SSE turn stream inside \`ctx.waitUntil\`. The runtime cancels waitUntil tasks ~30s after the ACK response ends, and **cancellation is not an exception**: no \`turn.failed\`, no \`onTurnError\`, no \`_(the turn failed)_\` — the DO's \`/turn\` shows \`Canceled\` and the thread shows nothing.

Live-reproduced on a production agent (kaik-crisp-agent, 2026-07-29): a multi-round Q&A mention turn ran past the ceiling and evaporated —

```
POST /channels/slack - Ok @ 5:43:51
  (warn) waitUntil() tasks did not complete within the allowed time
         after invocation end and have been cancelled.
POST https://do/turn - Canceled @ 5:43:51
```

\`?detach=1\` (#77) already rescued *reply-dropping* shadow turns; reply-*bearing* turns had no escape.

## The fix — deliver=1, runDetached's reply-bearing sibling

Stays inside the RFC's design language (§9's \`channel.deliver()\` is the renderer; §11 gains the caveat + addendum):

- **\`POST /turn?deliver=1\`** (AgentDurableObject): 202 on acceptance, then the DO renders the turn's TurnEvent stream through the **source channel's own \`deliver()\`** (resolved from \`DoAgentDef.channels\` with the DO's env) under the DO's own lifetime. The reply target is derived from the inbound event (author/thread — exactly \`renderStream\`'s surface).
- **Capability refused with a 501 *before* the turn starts.** That ordering is the contract: the caller may fall back to consumer-side rendering knowing it cannot double-run the turn.
- **\`ctx.runDelivered\`** (ChannelContext, provided by \`durableChannelSurface\`) exposes it; a 501 maps to the typed **\`DeliverUnsupportedError\`**.
- **slackChannel** prefers \`ctx.runDelivered\` on the streaming respondTo path; falls back to worker-side \`renderStream\` only on \`DeliverUnsupportedError\` (any other rejection is ambiguous — the turn may already run — and must not re-run).
- **\`observeTurnEvents\`**: \`sseTurnStream\`'s in-process sibling — eager subscription (same no-missed-event timing guarantee), buffered, terminal-closed, unsubscribes on early consumer exit.

## Adoption on the durable edge

Pass the same channel factories to the DO — \`new AgentDurableObject(ctx, { …, channels: [slackChannel], env })\`. Without that the channel falls back to the old (ceiling-bounded) worker-side rendering by design.

## Not in scope (noted in RFC §11)

- HITL **resume** continuations still render worker-side (same ceiling) — tracked follow-up.
- crispChannel's reply path untouched (observe/shadow mode uses \`runDetached\`).

## Tests

- core: delivered preference, typed-error fallback, no-fallback on ambiguous errors (channels.test.ts)
- server: 202 + full stream through \`deliver()\` with event-derived target/session; pre-start 501 (transcript stays empty); 400 without an event; render-failure logging; surface 501 → \`DeliverUnsupportedError\` (agent-durable.test.ts)
- Full suite: **826 pass / 0 fail**; typecheck green across all packages. Changeset included (patch core + server).
